section_summary: This section moves from 1945 reports of Japanese espionage in China to a lengthy translated account of the Japanese Embassy Office in Shanghai and its internal rivalries. It then begins a set of reports on alleged Filipino collaborators in Shanghai, including statements about wartime associations, propaganda events, allegiance pledges, and arrests.

subfiles.title: Japanese Espionage
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese efforts to learn Chiang Kai-shek's policies through Chin Bu-Yoo and Ryuu Jitsu-Shuu.
subfiles.summary: Reports alleged access to Ch'en Li-Fu's proposals concerning postwar self-government for colonies.

subfiles.title: Confidential quotation concerning Japanese espionage
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, American Mission, Chungking
subfiles.about: Passes on the February 19 confidential report about Japanese espionage and Ch'en Li-Fu's proposals.
subfiles.summary: Quotes the source's report for the mission's confidential information.

subfiles.title: Japanese secret societies activities
subfiles.about: Points to another file's summary of activities attributed to Japanese secret societies.
subfiles.summary: References original paper no. 131 in Pacific War file 740.0011.

subfiles.title: Further Developments in Case Evidently Involving Espionage for the Japanese by First War Zone Officers
subfiles.from: Edward Rice, Second Secretary of Embassy, Sian
subfiles.to: Patrick J. Hurley, American Ambassador, Chungking
subfiles.about: Relays Tu Ch'ang-ch'eng's account of alleged Japanese agents among senior First War Zone officers.
subfiles.summary: Rice reports that Wen Ch'iang acknowledged accusations against General Wang Tse-ming but told Tu to abandon the case. The account also alleges an espionage network of about fifty names and heroin traffic from occupied Shanxi.

subfiles.title: Distribution of Sian espionage despatch
subfiles.to: Military Intelligence Division; Office of Naval Intelligence; Federal Bureau of Investigation; Office of Strategic Services
subfiles.about: Distributes the Sian despatch on First War Zone officers.
subfiles.summary: Lists intelligence recipients of the attached information.

subfiles.title: SINTIC Item 343: Japanese Embassy Office in Shanghai
subfiles.from: Sino Translation and Interrogation Center, China Theater
subfiles.to: United States military and intelligence recipients
subfiles.about: Introduces a translation on the organization and activities of the Japanese Embassy Office in Shanghai.
subfiles.summary: The cover characterizes the office as a Greater East Asia Ministry agency and notes friction among Japanese government departments.

subfiles.title: Activities of the Shanghai Office of the Japanese Embassy (Central China Area)
subfiles.from: Former employee of the Japanese Embassy Office in Shanghai; translated by SINTIC
subfiles.about: Describes the office's origins, organization, wartime activities, and conflicts among Japanese civilian and military officials.
subfiles.summary: The report traces the transition from the Asia Promotion Board's Central China Liaison Bureau to the Shanghai Embassy Office under the Greater East Asia Ministry. It lists personnel and departmental functions, then describes competition among the army, navy, Foreign Office, and other ministries over administration and the “New Policy Towards China.” It also discusses failures of Japanese economic and cultural policy and Counsellor Okazaki's limited mediating role. The translation explicitly notes that the source contains no Report III.

subfiles.title: Reports on Filipino Collaborators in China
subfiles.from: Franklin P. Holcomb, Strategic Services Unit
subfiles.to: Jack D. Neal, Department of State
subfiles.about: Forwards a list and thirty-four reports on Filipino collaborators in China.
subfiles.summary: Notes that prior State Department distribution is unknown.

subfiles.title: Reports on Filipino Collaborators in China
subfiles.about: Lists subjects of the attached Filipino collaborator reports.
subfiles.summary: Alphabetical name list with cross-references to Luis Blanco.

subfiles.title: Gregorio Abelardo
subfiles.from: Shanghai investigators; statements by Gregorio Abelardo and H. Evangelista
subfiles.about: Assesses Abelardo's activities in Japanese-sponsored Filipino organizations and independence celebrations.
subfiles.summary: Abelardo describes association meetings and his prayer at the 1943 independence ceremony. Evangelista calls him pro-Japanese; the report records his allegiance pledge, association membership, and signatures on petitions supporting the Co-Prosperity Sphere.

subfiles.title: Florencio Alvarez
subfiles.from: Shanghai investigators; statements by Florencio Alvarez and H. Evangelista
subfiles.about: Assesses musician Florencio Alvarez's participation in Filipino Association and Japanese-sponsored activities.
subfiles.summary: Alvarez describes coerced attendance, his music work, and an independence pledge; Evangelista disputes his account. The report documents signed petitions and resolutions, participation in the 1943 parade, and allegiance to the wartime Philippine government.

subfiles.title: Claro Asuncion
subfiles.doc_type: investigative report with statements and exhibits
subfiles.from: Shanghai investigators; statements by Claro Asuncion and witnesses
subfiles.about: Examines Asuncion's Filipino Association leadership, Japanese-sponsored events, petitions, and alleged part in arrests.
subfiles.summary: Asuncion recounts his association work, independence pledge, Nanjing youth rally, and contacts with Japanese officials while denying anti-American activity or knowledge of arrests. The report reproduces his radio address and petitions, then presents conflicting accounts from Sara Malabanan, H. Evangelista, P. C. Espino, Primitivo Cruz, and others linking him to collaboration and arrests. The document continues beyond page 45.
